Applicability.description:
How much a fix may be trusted, which is what decides whether `--fix` applies it.

A safe fix cannot lose the author's work, an unsafe fix can, and a display fix is a change only
a person can make, so it is printed and never applied.
Applicability.title: Applicability

Certainty.description:
Whether a finding is wrong for sure or only probably wrong.

The threshold a run fails on is `--fail-on`, which names a threshold and never a field value, so
these two words are read and never compared against a flag.
Certainty.title: Certainty

Code.description:
Every judgement DeckTalk can make, with its sentence, its certainty and what decides it.

The member name is the code an agent dispatches on and passes to `--allow`. The prefix is the
subject the finding judges, which groups the codes for sorting, for `--allow` and for the docs
URL. `decides` names the settings keys whose values move the verdict, so an agent that meets a
code knows which knob to read without a second call.
Code.title: Code

CommandFix.description: A fix that runs a command, which is the whole argv a caller may hand to a subprocess.

kind.description: The kind of fix, which is how a reader dispatches on it.
kind.title: Kind

title.description: One sentence saying what applying this fix does.
title.title: Title

applicability.description: Whether this fix may be applied without asking.

command.description: The command to run, one argument per element.
command.title: Command

CommandFix.title: CommandFix

Edit.description:
One change to one file, named by exactly one locator so an agent can apply it without guessing.

A pointer addresses a place in a JSON file, a key addresses a place in a TOML file, and a line
addresses a place in any other text file.

file.description: The file this edit changes, project-relative.
file.title: File

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into that file, or null.
pointer.title: Pointer

key.description: A dotted TOML key in that file, or null.
key.title: Key

line.description: A line number in that file, or null.
line.title: Line

old.description: What is there now, or null when the edit only adds.
old.title: Old

new.description: What goes there instead, which is the empty string when the edit removes.
new.title: New

Edit.title: Edit

EditFix.description: A fix that changes files, which is what scaffolds a missing cue row or repairs a phrase.

kind.description: The kind of fix, which is how a reader dispatches on it.
kind.title: Kind

title.description: One sentence saying what applying this fix does.
title.title: Title

applicability.description: Whether this fix may be applied without asking.

edits.description: Every change this fix makes, applied together or not at all.
edits.title: Edits

EditFix.title: EditFix

ErrorCode.description:
Why DeckTalk could not run, with the sentence a reader meets and the exit code it takes.

The value is the code as JSON writes it and as the docs URL spells it. Each is a noun naming
what is missing or wrong, never an imperative naming what the tool wishes the caller would do.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

ErrorInfo.description:
The `error` of a result: why the command could not run, and what would let it.

It is filled only when the command could not run at all, so a reader that finds it null knows
the command ran and that every judgement is in `findings`.

code.description: The code a caller dispatches on, such as NOT_BUILT.

message.description: One sentence saying what is wrong, with the measured detail in it.
message.title: Message

hint.description: The whole command that would clear this, or null.
hint.title: Hint

location.description: The file and line to open, or null.

docs.description: The docs page for this code.
docs.title: Docs

ErrorInfo.title: ErrorInfo

Finding.description:
One judgement, in the shape every renderer, every schema and every agent receives.

`certainty` and `url` are the code's own and are written into the object rather than left for a
reader to look up, so one line of JSON carries everything a decision needs. A raiser leaves them
out and the code fills them, and a value that disagrees with the code is refused. Both therefore
carry a declared default, which says in the signature and in the schema that a raiser names the
code and nothing else. Neither default is ever the value in force, because the code fills both
before this model is built and refuses any finding whose code it does not know.

code.description: The stable code a caller dispatches on, such as CUE_OFF.

message.description: One sentence, with every measured number and its limit written into it.
message.title: Message

certainty.description: Whether this is wrong for sure or only probably wrong.

location.description: The object this judges, with its file, line, section and cue.

stage.description: The stage that raised it, or null when no stage did.

fix.description: A change that resolves it, or null when none is known.
fix.title: Fix

url.description: The docs page for this code.
url.title: Url

Finding.title: Finding

Layer.description:
Which of the five layers set a settings value, lowest first.

A key with no override is set by `default`, which is also what refuses `--max-cost` on a price
nobody has stated: DeckTalk would be capping a spend against a number it made up.
Layer.title: Layer

Location.description:
Where a finding is, as the five facts that travel together into a renderer and into a fix.

`where` is never null, because the object a finding judges is what tells a reader which side of
the spend it came from, and the other four are filled by whoever knows them.

where.description: The object this finding judges, such as a cue id, a slide or a file.
where.title: Where

file.description: The file to open, project-relative, or null.
file.title: File

line.description: The line in that file, counting from one, or null.
line.title: Line

section.description: The section number this is about, or null.
section.title: Section

cue.description: The wire id of the cue this is about, or null.
cue.title: Cue

Location.title: Location

file.title: File

hash.description: The content hash that decides whether a take may be reused.
hash.title: Hash

SectionTake.title: SectionTake

SettingFix.description: A fix that turns a knob, which is the same key space `config set` and `--set` take.

kind.description: The kind of fix, which is how a reader dispatches on it.
kind.title: Kind

title.description: One sentence saying what applying this fix does.
title.title: Title

applicability.description: Whether this fix may be applied without asking.

key.description: The settings key to set, such as verify.cue_offset_max_ms.
key.title: Key

value.description: The value to set it to, spelled as a command line would spell it.
value.title: Value

SettingFix.title: SettingFix

Spend.description:
What a run costs, priced once so a caller never works it out from a character count.

`--max-cost` is compared against `ceiling_dollars` and never against `dollars`, because credits
are consumed one request at a time and a cap that claimed to stop a run halfway would be a lie.

state.description: Whether this is what the run would cost or what it did cost.

sections.description: The sections this price covers, in script order.

items.description: The section this row is about, as the author numbered it.

sections.title: Sections

characters.description: How many characters of script this price is for.
characters.title: Characters

dollars.description: The price at the stated rate, in US dollars.
dollars.title: Dollars

ceiling_dollars.description: The most this run can cost, in US dollars.
ceiling_dollars.title: Ceiling Dollars

price_per_1000_characters.description: The rate this price was worked out at.
price_per_1000_characters.title: Price Per 1000 Characters

price_layer.description: Which layer set that rate, where default means nobody stated it.

Spend.title: Spend

SpendState.description: Whether a price is what a run would cost or what it did cost.
SpendState.title: SpendState

Stage.description: One stage of the pipeline, declared in run order. The value is the word that names it.

TakeStatus.description: What one run did about one section's take.

ok.description: True when the command ran and judged nothing certain.

sections.title: Sections

spend.description: What this run cost, or would have cost.

takes.description: The take index this run wrote, or null on a dry run.
takes.title: Takes

seconds.title: Seconds
